prompt.context: You are given two hourglasses — one measures 7 minutes and the other measures 4 minutes.
prompt.question: How would you use the two hourglasses to measure a continuous time period of exactly 9 minutes? You have 10 minutes to derive your answer.

framework: Label the 7-minute hourglass as I and the 4-minute hourglass as II
Track elapsed time at each state transition
Identify when a flip of one glass can bridge the remaining gap to 9 minutes

questions.prompt: Walk through the exact sequence of steps to measure 9 continuous minutes using the two hourglasses.
questions.guidance: A strong answer enumerates each action (start, flip) and the cumulative elapsed time at each step, arriving cleanly at 9 minutes without any gap in counting.

math.setup: I = 7-min hourglass, II = 4-min hourglass. Start both simultaneously at t=0 and track remaining sand in each glass.
steps: t=0: Flip both I and II simultaneously. Start timing.
t=4: II expires. Flip II over immediately. (I has 3 min of sand remaining.)
t=7: I expires. Flip I over immediately. (II has 1 min of sand remaining.)
t=8: II expires. Flip I over immediately. (I has just been running for 1 min, so 6 min of sand remain.)
t=9: I expires. Exactly 9 minutes have elapsed since t=0.

recommendation: Turn both hourglasses over at the same moment (t=0)
Flip II when it runs out at t=4
Flip I when it runs out at t=7
Flip I again when II runs out at t=8
Stop timing when I runs out at t=9 — exactly 9 continuous minutes have been measured
risks: Any delay between a glass expiring and the flip breaks the continuous count
The method requires no gap between step transitions
